newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 1.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
- BLAIR ON BRINK OF A LANDSLIDE

A last minute poll for MORI for the Evening Standard shows that Tony Blair is set for a landslide Labour victory. The only change that potential voters showed is that some are switching allegiance to the Liberal Democrats.
- ING BARINGS TALKS TO BUY US BANKERS

The US investment banking boutique Dillon Read is set to be bought by ING Barings the Dutch controlled bank. The companies are in advanced negotiations at the moment. ING Barings is set to pay between 425mn (262mn stg) and 450 US dollars for the 75 percent of Dillon Read it does not currently own.
- STERLING JUNK FIRST FROM BBC TRANSMISSION

City history books are to be made when BBC Home Service transmission network becomes the first company to issue junk bonds in sterling. Castle Transmission, an American led consortium assembled to buy the network for around 250mn in February. Credit Suisse First Boston and JP Morgan are arranging a 100mn issue for the company.
- MURDOCH SATELLITE DREAM FADES IN US

Murdoch's attempts to break into the competitive world of television distribution in the US have so far failed in ASkyB, the 3bn US dollar US satellite TV system that News Corp hopes will be a complementary service to BSkyB.

Two pensioners who claim that National Grid creamed off monies from a surplus in its pension scheme, will find out today whether they can go ahead with a legal challenge which could cost the electricity industry 1.5bn stg.
